Marcelo

messages.subject_clean: Plotting Cumulative Score Category Functions for GRMs
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

Hope all is well. I am wondering if there is a way to create empirical plots of cumulative score category functions using the itemfit function (or another mirt function) for items scaled with a unidimensional graded response model? In the itemfit function, I am only able to create empirical plots of the score category functions vs cumulative score category functions. The latter would be helpful in being able to see if there is any misfit due to violation of the assumption of equal slopes across categories; and also would love to be able to use the CI function built into itemfit for dichotomous items on the plotted cumulative score category functions if possible. Any thoughts are much appreciated.

Thank you,
Keri

messages.subject: Re: 2 Questions: Subset of questions continuous responses and invariance specifications with n>2 groups
messages.subject_clean: 2 Questions: Subset of questions continuous responses and invariance specifications with n>2 groups
messages.body_plain:
Hi Emma,

Sorry it took me so long to reply to your email. I recently made a rather abrupt international move back to Canada, so much of my life was put on hold for nearly two months. Fortunately, it's finally starting to smooth out again.

Regarding your questions. Currently, mirt cannot deal with continuous response formats. That's not to say it couldn't, as theoretically this is possible. I agree without your current approach though to truncating the continuous measure into something with fewer parameters, particularly if you have a smaller sample size. Regarding the 10 size recommendation, that has more to do with your sample size and frequency of the collapsed categories than anything else (you don't want the binned categories to be too small, otherwise intercept parameter estimates can be very large and unstable).

>
> My second question relates to the specification of anchor items and parameter invariance across a larger number of groups. An example of the structure of groups and questions is shown in the image attached. Sets of questions are wide and groups of individuals are long. Filled in blocks are where a group answered that group of questions, NA blocks are questions that did not get asked to a specific group. I understand that for the two group case, for questions that were asked to one group and not the other, I would want to specify the column names in the invariance argument, so that only one set of parameters would be estimated. However, how would you handle the three group case, where I want different parameters estimated for two of the groups (because there is evidence that the question functions differently between those two groups) but for the third group I don't really want any parameters estimated because the group was not administered those questions.

You can set the third groups parameters to be equal to either the first or second groups; it makes no difference in the estimation because the third group does not contribute to the likelihood equations. For this setup, you may find it easier to work with the complete syntax form documented in ?mirt.model, which should help you with the parameter equivalence specification (see the [ ] notation to explicitly select groups).

> Additionally, there could be a case in which all three groups are administered the same question and for two of the groups the parameters should be estimated as the same, but for the third group there is DIF and different parameters should be estimated. Ideally, instead of specifying invariance as column names, it would make sense if the specification could be a matrix that would tell you where parameter values could differ across groups and questions. Can you think of a way that I could handle this type of structure in mirt? If not possible in mirt, do you know of other software that would be able to handle this?

Yes, see the mirt.model() syntax for this as well. Cheers.

Phil

>
> Thanks so much,
> Emma

messages.subject: "NA" values for some beta estimates in polyCAT
messages.subject_clean: "NA" values for some beta estimates in polyCAT
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I apologize if this comes off as a beginner question, as I am just getting started with mirt and CAT. I ran the mirt function for a simulated 5-item polytomous response pattern using a GPCM model. However, some of the betas for the response options were "NA." I've produced the parameters for the first 10 questions, as reference.

id a b1 b2 b3 b4
1 2.188891 0.799167 0.171552 -0.4231 NA
2 3.116017 0.289836 -0.45773 -0.36974 NA
3 3.363451 -0.07045 -0.09065 0.07369 0.040219
4 2.604773 -0.28404 -0.20778 -0.09344 0.42448
5 2.307046 -0.60988 0.165687 NA NA
6 2.477962 0.108575 0.308608 -0.03472 0.061221
7 3.512669 0.101464 -0.28706 0.436758 0.413581
8 3.225537 0.283565 0.420048 0.239907 -0.32759
9 2.571879 -0.11952 -0.49139 -0.1683 -0.26689
10 2.870999 -0.01151 NA NA NA

I've read a few papers, and some papers produce IRT parameters with no missing values, while others produce IRT parameters with some "NA"s, like mine above. Is there a way to produce a full set of IRT parameters without any missing parameters? Thank you.

messages.subject_clean: "NA" values for some beta estimates in polyCAT
messages.body_plain:
The NAs are just placholders. E.g., item 1 seems to have 4 response categories observed, while item 3 has 5 response categories observed. If you have categories that were not endorsed then the intercepts/difficult parameters would not be identified for those categories, and in mirt these are structurally ignored. HTH.

Phil

messages.subject: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test
messages.subject_clean: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

In our development of a CAT, we had originally adapted a typical 5-point Likert scale using a polytomous IRT model. However, we have recently decided to change this to a Yes/No dichotmous IRT model. This wouldn't normally be a problem, but most dichotmous IRT models assess Correct/Incorrect choices (e.g. "Is 2 + 2 = 4?), whereas our model assess Yes/No responses (e.g. "Are you able to walk?), which doesn't have a "correct" answer. Would approaching this design as a "two-item" polytomous model using mirt be applicable? This would only generate 1 B parameter per question. I am a bit confused as I rarely see a "two-item" Likert scale, and a Yes/No response isn't really ordinal. Any help would be appreciated, thank you.

messages.subject: Re: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test
messages.subject_clean: Using mirt for dichotomous item-response test
messages.body_plain:
You can think of the outcome you are modeling as the "yes" (or analogously the "correct") response. If your scale is modeling physical functioning ability, with higher scores indicating more physical functioning, then you can apply a 1PL or 2PL IRT model to these items, which are appropriate for dichotomous response categories. So in essence your IRT model would be estimating the probability of a "yes" response to each item given particular item characteristics (i.e., item difficulty if using a 1PL or both item difficulty and discrimination if using a 2PL)...

Keri

> Hi Emma,
>
> Sorry it took me so long to reply to your email. I recently made a rather abrupt international move back to Canada, so much of my life was put on hold for nearly two months. Fortunately, it's finally starting to smooth out again.
>
> Regarding your questions. Currently, mirt cannot deal with continuous response formats. That's not to say it couldn't, as theoretically this is possible. I agree without your current approach though to truncating the continuous measure into something with fewer parameters, particularly if you have a smaller sample size. Regarding the 10 size recommendation, that has more to do with your sample size and frequency of the collapsed categories than anything else (you don't want the binned categories to be too small, otherwise intercept parameter estimates can be very large and unstable).
>
> >
> > My second question relates to the specification of anchor items and parameter invariance across a larger number of groups. An example of the structure of groups and questions is shown in the image attached. Sets of questions are wide and groups of individuals are long. Filled in blocks are where a group answered that group of questions, NA blocks are questions that did not get asked to a specific group. I understand that for the two group case, for questions that were asked to one group and not the other, I would want to specify the column names in the invariance argument, so that only one set of parameters would be estimated. However, how would you handle the three group case, where I want different parameters estimated for two of the groups (because there is evidence that the question functions differently between those two groups) but for the third group I don't really want any parameters estimated because the group was not administered those questions.
>
> You can set the third groups parameters to be equal to either the first or second groups; it makes no difference in the estimation because the third group does not contribute to the likelihood equations. For this setup, you may find it easier to work with the complete syntax form documented in ?mirt.model, which should help you with the parameter equivalence specification (see the [ ] notation to explicitly select groups).
>
>
> > Additionally, there could be a case in which all three groups are administered the same question and for two of the groups the parameters should be estimated as the same, but for the third group there is DIF and different parameters should be estimated. Ideally, instead of specifying invariance as column names, it would make sense if the specification could be a matrix that would tell you where parameter values could differ across groups and questions. Can you think of a way that I could handle this type of structure in mirt? If not possible in mirt, do you know of other software that would be able to handle this?
>

messages.body_plain:
Hello, all,

Please be gentle to me as I mainly use Stata, and I'm starting to convert to R. I'll be using the mirt package for my dissertation.

In much of my work, I've found it very useful to use dot and whisker plots of regression coefficients, as the the R package dotwhisker <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dotwhisker/vignettes/dotwhisker-vignette.html> does. I intend to used mixedmirt to fit a regression to an IRT-estimated latent trait, and I don't see any functionality native to mixedmirt that would enable me to plot the regression coefficients (as opposed to the item characteristic curves and such). I also know that dotwhisker won't accept objects of the classes produced by mixedmirt. Does anyone have suggestions how to plot regression coefficients from mixedmirt?

Also, the above-mentioned latent trait is depression. Unipolar IRT models like the log-logistic model have been proposed for unipolar traits like depression and other forms of psychopathology. In health services research, which is my field, I believe a lot of the traits we're interested in are better modeled by unipolar models, rather than bipolar models. If unipolar models aren't on Phil's radar already, I'd love to put them on, and ask if he'd consider implementing them in the future.

messages.subject: Re: Constraining factor loadings to be the same for identification purposes in bifactor model
messages.subject_clean: Constraining factor loadings to be the same for identification purposes in bifactor model
messages.body_plain:
The documentation for the third argument is this:

model2   a two-tier model specification object defined by mirt.model() or a string to be passed to mirt.model. By default the model will fit a unidimensional model in the second-tier, and therefore be equivalent to the bifactor model

So, by default this is something like model2 = "G=1-7". If you omit this 'G' factor then the general factor is not created, and only the orthogonal specific factors are modeled (which is kind of useless; it makes more sense just to estimate separate unidimensional models if that's the case). You need to keep the G structure in the model, and add your constraints here as well since the specific terms are added automagically.

specific <- c(rep(1,5),rep(2,2))
model <- "G=1-7

                CONSTRAIN = (6-7, a3)"

modbifactor <- bfactor (dataset, specific, model)

HTH.

Phil
